question.problem:
Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ and $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}.$ 
What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={c}_{1}+{c}_{2}-{c}_{3}, \\ {b}_{2} & =2{c}_{3}+{c}_{2}, \\ {b}_{3} & =-{c}_{3}+2{c}_{1},\end{aligned}
$$

and  the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & a & b \\ -1 & 2 & c\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C$ are

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{3}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=0,$ and $c=-1.$
